                    [32m'            }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    if (routePath.indexOf("**") !== -1) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        throw new Error(`RedwoodSDK: Invalid route pattern: "${routePath}" contains "**". Use "*" for a single wildcard segment. Double wildcards are not supported.`);\n'[39m +

                    [32m'        return result;\n'[39m +

                    [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        else {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    };\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    pathCache.set(routePath, result);\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return result;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export function matchPath(routePath, requestPath) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    const compiled = compilePath(routePath);\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    if (compiled.isStatic) {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'        const param = compiled.paramMap[i];\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        params[param.name] = matches[i + 1];\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return params;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function flattenRoutes(routes) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return routes.reduce((acc, route) => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        if (Array.isArray(route)) {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'}\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    });\n'[39m +

                [32m"* Configure a D1 binding named `DB` in `wrangler.jsonc`, wire up Drizzle's `drizzle-orm/d1` driver, define your schema, and generate migrations with `drizzle-kit` so the schema can be applied to the local D1 database.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Return `Response` objects with an `application/json` content type and the appropriate HTTP status codes.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Runtime & API Contract\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Project path: `/home/user/project`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The Cloudflare D1 binding MUST be named `DB`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Database migrations must be generatable/appliable against the local D1 database (a Drizzle migration must exist in the repository).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Start command: `npm run dev`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Port: `5173`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Data model\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Each user has:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `id`: integer, auto-generated, unique, monotonically increasing in insertion order.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `name`: string, required.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `email`: string, required, unique.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Endpoints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'#### `GET /api/users`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Lists users ordered by `id` ascending (i.e. oldest created first).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Query parameters (both optional):\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `limit`: maximum number of users to return. Defaults to `10` when omitted.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `offset`: number of users to skip from the start. Defaults to `0` when omitted.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'On success returns status `200` with a JSON body:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "users": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    { "id": number, "name": string, "email": string }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "total": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "limit": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "offset": number\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Where `users` is the requested page (respecting `limit` and `offset`), `total` is the total number of users in the database (independent of pagination), and `limit`/`offset` echo the effective values used for the query.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'#### `POST /api/users`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Creates a new user.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Request body (JSON):\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{ "name": string, "email": string }\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* On success returns status `201` with the created user as JSON: `{ "id": number, "name": string, "email": string }`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* If `name` or `email` is missing or empty, returns status `400`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* If a user with the same `email` already exists, returns status `409`.'[39m
            }

Follow the principle of least privilege\\n6. Implement proper security headers and CORS policies\\n7. Optimize for performance with caching strategies\\n\\n## What is Middleware?\\n\\nMiddleware functions in RedwoodSDK are functions that run on every request before your route handlers. They can:\\n\\n- Add security headers\\n- Handle CORS\\n- Implement caching strategies\\n- Add request/response logging\\n- Transform request/response data\\n- Implement rate limiting\\n- Add performance monitoring\\n- Handle error boundaries\\n- Setup sessions\\n- Authenticate users\\n\\n## Example Templates\\n\\n### Basic Middleware Structure\\n\\n```tsx\\nexport default defineApp([\\n  setCommonHeaders(),\\n  async ({ ctx, request, response }) => {\\n    await setupDb(env);\\n    setupSessionStore(env);\\n    try {\\n      // Grab the session\'s data.\\n      ctx.session = await sessions.load(request);\\n    } catch (error) {\\n      if (error instanceof ErrorResponse && error.code === 401) {\\n        await sessions.remove(request, response.headers);\\n        response.headers.set(\\"Location\\", \\"/user/login\\");\\n\\n        return new Response(null, {\\n          status: 302,\\n          headers: response.headers,\\n        });\\n      }\\n\\n      throw error;\\n    }\\n\\n    // Populate the ctx with the user\'s data\\n    if (ctx.session?.userId) {\\n      ctx.user = await db.user.findUnique({\\n        where: {\\n          id: ctx.session.userId,\\n        },\\n      });\\n    }\\n  },\\n  // Route handlers\\n]);\\n```\\n";'[39m

                    [32m'            function renderElement(element) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'                const requestInfo = getRequestInfo();\n'[39m +

                    [32m'                const elementType = element.type;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'                const componentName = typeof elementType === "function" && elementType.name\n'[39m +
                    [32m'                    ? elementType.name\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).             [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
